Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope and source array contain only standard, expected operations. The `source` array fetches two files from the package's own upstream repository on GitHub: a release tarball from `github.com/SulfurNitride/Fluorine-Manager/releases` and a LICENSE file from `raw.githubusercontent.com/SulfurNitride/Fluorine-Manager`. Both URLs match the declared `url` field, confirming they are legitimate upstream sources. The checksums are real SHA256 hashes (not SKIP), and `pkgver` is set as a plain string variable (`0.3.3`) rather than computed by a `pkgver()` function, so no build-time code executes during sourcing.

No command substitution (`$(...)`, backticks), `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or other potentially dangerous constructs appear in the top-level scope. The `_releaseArchive` variable and `source` array use only standard variable expansion (`$pkgver`), which poses no execution risk. The `build()` and `package()` functions contain `sed` patches to the wrapper script, but these are out of scope since `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` prevent their execution during the specified commands.

Extraction of the downloaded tarball will write files to disk but will not execute them, which is the intended behavior of these audit commands. There is no evidence of injected malicious code that would execute during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Sources from own GitHub upstream; no malicious top-level code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: a release tarball and a LICENSE file, both fetched from the project's official GitHub repository using HTTPS. The `sha256sums` are provided and match the expected integrity checks for the sources. No top-level command substitutions, dynamic sourcing, or immediate execution of downloaded content occurs outside of the `build()` and `package()` functions, which are not executed under `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`.

The `pkgver` is hardcoded to `0.3.3`, so no external calls (e.g., curl, git) are made during sourcing to determine the version. There are no calls to `git clone`, `curl | bash`, `eval`, or any other dangerous constructs in the global scope or in `pkgver()`. The variables used in `source` are simple string interpolations based on `$pkgver` and do not introduce remote code execution risks during source fetching.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch and extract the declared sources without executing any potentially malicious code.
</details>

All operations are confined to the package directory (`$pkgdir`) and follow Arch Linux packaging guidelines. There are no dangerous commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, or remote code execution), no unexpected file access, and no suspicious environment manipulation. The package provides a legitimate integration of a third-party binary into the Arch ecosystem.
